children.value: Review rubric for agent pull requests
Use this page when reviewing a pull request that a coding agent opened, or when an agent self-checks before it asks for review. CI (
and the jobs behind it) already enforces build, tests, coverage floors, quality targets, generated-file drift, and the self-scan. This rubric covers what those checks cannot see.

Walk the four checks below on the diff. Record a request for changes when a
item fails; leave nits as non-blocking comments.
Agents opening a pull request run the same four checks on their own diff and fix block failures before requesting review.
Does the change match the issue, and only the issue?
for one task issue, and the diff matches that brief
A second issue's work is bundled in, or the body closes an epic
list (plus tests, changelog fragments, and regenerations the brief's steps require)
Unrelated refactors, drive-by formatting, or files the brief forbids
Network on a scan path, executing repository or fixture code, hand-edited generated output, or an unsourced dependency add
Extra work is named as a new issue, not shipped in this diff
Scope grew "while we were here" without a new issue
Does each change sit in the layer that owns it? See
Engine, SDK, detectors, registry, source-usage, and adapters stay inside their "Owns" / "Must not" rows
A detector makes a network call; an adapter owns rule or migration logic; the engine imports a built-in detector or grows ecosystem-specific branches
Additive change only, or a numbered decision under
Repository contents are parsed, never evaluated; scans stay offline
New code executes scanned input, or a scan path gains network access
Assembled registries are regenerated from per-item sources; generated trees are rebuilt with the commands in AGENTS.md
, assembled thresholds, or other generated outputs
Do the tests prove the behavior the issue asked for? Use
A new or changed behavior has a test that fails without the change and asserts a finding, exit code, JSON field, or rendered output
No test for a behavior change, or the test only asserts that a private helper was called
The smallest suitable kind from TESTING.md carries the proof
An end-to-end spawn is used where a unit or detector test would see the bug
Assertions avoid clocks, absolute temp paths, and unordered maps; paths are cross-platform
paths, or real sleeps waiting on the system under test
Fixtures are parsed, not executed; no network on the test path except where a command is explicitly about the network
The test runs fixture code, hits a registry, or weakens a floor/threshold to land the change
Docs-only and pure chore changes that cannot affect runtime behavior need no new test; say so in the pull request.
Do the words match what the code and data actually do?
User-visible behavior, flags, and contracts are documented in the same pull request
Docs promise a flag, tool, or guarantee the diff does not implement
Lifecycle claims cite an authoritative, versioned source; status is never inferred from popularity or "a newer version exists"
A rule, README line, or migration step invents a status or replacement
Reference, answer, OG, and plugin pages were regenerated from source when the source changed
Generated pages were edited by hand or left stale
fragment exists for user-visible behavior; docs/test/ci/chore changes correctly omit one
A user-visible change ships without a fragment, or
Any of the following is enough to request changes. Do not approve until it is fixed or the issue brief is updated and the pull request matches it.
fails on the commit under review.
: work outside the issue brief, a second issue bundled in, or a "Do not" violation.
: wrong layer ownership, scan/network/exec trust rule broken, or a public-contract break without a decision record.
: behavior changed with no failing-first test, or tests that only exercise mocks/internals while the product path stays unasserted.
: overclaimed lifecycle status, undocumented user-visible change, hand-edited generated files, or a missing changelog fragment for user-visible behavior.
: allowlist raised or extended to make the change pass, new
, or a file/function over the ceilings without an existing allowlist entry that this change is not allowed to add.
: a new runtime dependency or GitHub Action that Offing would report as end-of-life, deprecated, or retired, or one added with no reason in the pull request.
Nits (wording, optional renames, style that already matches surrounding code) must not block a merge. Ask for them in a follow-up issue when they are worth doing.
This rubric is a living checklist. After it has been applied to

agent pull requests, update this page from what those reviews showed: drop checks CI now covers, sharpen checks that caught real defects, and add checks that reviewers had to invent ad hoc. Record the pass in the table below so the adjustment is evidence-backed, not vibes.
What the rubric caught or missed
When row 10 is filled, open a follow-up pull request that edits this page from the notes and clears or replaces the table for the next round.
